subject: Renewal: EU residency + APAC warm-seeding / seat reallocation discussion
content:
From: Satoshi Yamada <satoshi.yamada@medinex.co.jp>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 09:12:00 +0900
Subject: Renewal discussion - EU residency + APAC seeding options

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Medinex is approaching our renewal window (June 30) and the execs want to bundle two asks into the next term:

1) Formal EU residency (primary storage + processing in Frankfurt) for PHI-adjacent workloads.
2) A small APAC warm-seeding capability for pilot customers in Japan (we need standby capacity and cross-region failover precedence so EU is primary but APAC can accept traffic in failover).

We also want guidance on seat reallocation — we expect a 15% uplift in peak Q4 traffic and may reassign seats from our existing North America pool to the EU primary pool. Can you share a draft SOW and a ballpark for the top-up (monthly committed GPU-hours + warm-standby rate)?

Attaching a short scoping note internally.

Best,
Satoshi
Director, Cloud Ops
Medinex

----
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Satoshi Yamada <satoshi.yamada@medinex.co.jp>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Apr 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion - EU residency + APAC seeding options

Hi Satoshi — great to hear from you.

Short answer: we can do EU primary residency + an APAC warm-seeding lane with explicit failover precedence. A few clarifying points before we draft a SOW:

- Residency boundary: do you require EU-only processing (no token or audit metadata leaving region) or is log/metrics replication to US acceptable for operations?
- Failover precedence: should APAC be configured as "standby" only (accept traffic when EU is unreachable) or as a scheduled warm-burst for planned events?
- Seat reallocation: do you want permanent reassignments or a temporary commit (Q4 peak) with an option to revert?

I'll loop Ben (capacity/pricing) and Monica (onboarding/ops) for numbers and an initial SOW. If you can confirm the three clarifying points by EOD Monday (4/9) we can aim for a draft SOW the following week.

Thanks — Hannah
Head of Renewals, Redwood Inference
hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0199

----
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Satoshi Yamada <satoshi.yamada@medinex.co.jp>
Date: Fri, 6 Apr 2028 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion - EU residency + APAC seeding options

Thanks Satoshi — quick pricing sketch below (ballpark, subject to final SOW):

- EU primary residency tier: incremental +30% on hosted per-token pricing to cover EU-only storage/ops controls + onshore node premium.
- APAC warm-seed (standby lane): fixed monthly standby fee of $6,500 for a 2x warm pool (enough to handle ~150 r/s surge while warm) + per-minute failover execution fees when invoked.
- Seat reallocation: temporary top-up commit (3 months) priced at $2,000 per reserved seat/month; permanent reassignments need a 6-12 month commit with a 10% discount.

I'll attach a capacity worksheet (Seat-Reallocation-worksheet.csv) and a draft SOW v2 by end of day Monday.

-Ben
Senior Sales Director, Redwood Inference

----
From: Satoshi Yamada <satoshi.yamada@medinex.co.jp>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Amira Haddad <amira.haddad@medinex.co.jp>
Date: Mon, 9 Apr 2028 09:30:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion - EU residency + APAC seeding options

Hannah / Ben — thanks for the clarity.

Answers:
- Residency: EU processing + storage only. We cannot have token-level or PII-adjacent metadata stored outside the EU. Metrics/logging replication is acceptable but must be anonymized and aggregated.
- Failover precedence: standby only — APAC must be passive and only accept traffic on automatic failover or explicit failover request.
- Seat reallocation: prefer a temporary 3-month top-up to cover Q4 peak, with a review before making any permanent reassignments.

Please include the anonymization controls in the SOW. Looking forward to the draft.

Satoshi

----
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Satoshi Yamada <satoshi.yamada@medinex.co.jp>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion - EU residency + APAC seeding options

Satoshi — appreciated. Attached is the draft SOW (Redwood-APAC-seed-SOW-v2.pdf) and a Controls spreadsheet (Data-Residency-Controls.xlsx) that enumerates anonymization, KMS key locality, and audit log retention options.

Key callouts in the SOW:
- EU primary: data-at-rest and model KV cache pinned to the Frankfurt cluster; keys managed in customer-specific KMS in eu-central-1.
- Replication: operational metrics can be pushed to US ops but only as aggregated counters; raw request traces remain in EU.
- APAC warm lane: configured as passive; automatic health-triggered failover endpoint with a manual override process described in section 4.3.
- Pricing: includes Ben's standby fee sketch and seat top-up rows — see worksheet tab 'Q4_topup'.

Next step: Hannah — can we schedule a 45-min contract walkthrough with Medinex legal and our pricing/legal teams next week? I propose Wed 4/18 at 10am CEST (1am PT) — if that doesn't work I'll propose alternatives.

Thanks, Monica
Technical Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-APAC-seed-SOW-v2.pdf (application/pdf), Data-Residency-Controls.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

----
From: Satoshi Yamada <satoshi.yamada@medinex.co.jp>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Apr 2028 18:41:00 +0900
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion - EU residency + APAC seeding options

Monica — received, thank you. Reviewing with legal now; one ask: can the SOW call out the anonymization algorithm and minimum aggregation window for metrics forwarded outside EU? They need something explicit for their privacy officers.

Also — the DocuSign link for the current renewal is required by procurement to be live before May 20 to meet internal signatures. Can you confirm timeline for SOW to become an amendment to the renewal?

Regards,
Satoshi

----
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Satoshi Yamada <satoshi.yamada@medinex.co.jp>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Apr 2028 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion - EU residency + APAC seeding options

Satoshi — thanks for the prompt review. Quick update and commitments: 

- Monica will update section 3.1 of the SOW with explicit anonymization (SHA-256 hashing + 30-day rolling salt + minimum aggregation window of 15 minutes for exported metrics).
- Ben: we will confirm final standby fee and seat-topup pricing in the amendment. Targeting: APAC standby fee finalized and appended by EOD Friday (4/20).
- Legal/process: Lauren is looped for contract cadence — Lauren, can we commit to having the amendment routed to DocuSign by May 10 so Medinex procurement has time for signatures ahead of May 20?

Satoshi — once the amended SOW is in DocuSign we will mark it as an addendum to the existing renewal (MEDX-2028-RNW-71). That will preserve the June 30 term date and apply the top-up charges pro-rated from the roll date.

Next steps (summary):
- Monica: anonymization language + controls spreadsheet update (by 4/19).
- Ben: final pricing rows and Seat-Reallocation-worksheet update (by 4/20).
- Lauren: route amendment to DocuSign with internal approvals checklist (target to send by 5/10).
- Satoshi / Medinex: procurement review and signatures (target complete by 5/20).

I will stay owner for coordination. Thanks all — talk soon.

Best,
Hannah
Head of Renewals
